main_text.p: ragra, vel podagra cernitur, is non ex morbi essentia, sed ex vehementia fit doloris, qui ruborem, caloremque nonnunquam & febre accersit. Cum in primis ait ruborem & calorem nō ex morbi essentia, sed ex vehementia doloris fieri, tum udo sacco se ue-lat. Nam hæc omnia symptomata inflammationem necessario cōsequuntur. Quod ipsemet libro de Signis secundo testatur.Cap.10. Pars(inquit)quæ præter naturam, aut consuetudinem incaluit, sed ruber sanguine, si flauescit, bile præter modum perfusa est.» Hæc Fernelius è Galeni commentario in secundum Aphorismum, Sectionis primæ Hippocratis desumpta: ubi ait Galenus co-lorem cutis efflorescere similem humoribus in corpore redundantibus, nisi intrinsecus refluxerint. Deinde veterum authoritati, & rationi omnino resistit. In primis Galenus libro ad Glauconem inflammationem definiens calorem & ruborem ab inflammato sanguine effici aperte exprimit. Sanguine(inquit)optimo ac mediocriter crasso ad particulam aliquam confluente, atq; ob multitudinem conculcato, vehemens dolor arripit hominem, nisi he-betis sensus ipsa fuerit particula: pulsusq;

page.notes: Margin marks beside the first lines and beside "Pars(inquit)" to "perfusa est." are printed quotation marks; transcribed as ” / » (the scan shows small raised marks, exact glyph uncertain). Line-end hyphens "ue-lat", "co-lorem", "con-suetudinem", "he-betis" follow the printed hyphenation. The word "udo" read as printed; "fenfus"/"fuetudinem" read as sensus/suetudinem with long s as plain s. The first word "ragra" is a fragment continuing from the previous page. Catchword "in" and signature "Q 3" are printed at the foot.
